# Physics validation

`mrgym validate` runs 119 checks of engine `mrgym-engine-0.3.0`; all must pass, and the test suite asserts it. Each row compares the scanner with an analytic formula or with a calculation written separately from the engine.

What this establishes: the scanner computes the equations it states, to the bounds listed. What it does not: agreement with a measurement or with a real scanner. Rows whose reference was written by the same authors say so. Comparisons with another group's code and with published operating points: [external.md](external.md); with public measurements on real scanners: [measured.md](measured.md). Whether a simplification can change a scored answer is measured per environment by `mrgym validate --perturb <id>` and printed in the Validity section of the environment's card. References: [references.md](references.md). Simplifications: [limits.md](limits.md).

## Another group's simulator (optional, not in the test suite)

The RF-spoiled steady state of the engine (spgr and afi) against [sycomore](https://github.com/lamyj/sycomore), an extended phase graph simulator in C++ that is not a dependency of this package: 17 cases, largest difference 1.7e-12 of M0 without diffusion and 3.6e-10 with diffusion (bounds 1e-10 and 1e-07), on engine `mrgym-engine-0.2.0`, 2026-11-25. With diffusion both codes use the same b-factor formula, so this checks the implementation, not the diffusion model.

Regenerate: `pip install sycomore && python tools/external/compare_sycomore.py --write`.
